elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: "except no approval is required for assignment to a financially responsible affiliate" — retained from original and applies mutually, so Customer may assign to an affiliate without approval (subject to the pre-existing 'financially responsible' qualifier).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered carve-out covers "a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets" only; an assignment to a successor by acquisition (e.g., a stock purchase not structured as a merger) still requires the other party's prior written approval. To reach the preferred wording the drafter must add "acquisition" to the trigger list.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall assign or transfer its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party" — binds Vendor, so Vendor assignment requires Customer approval outside the affiliate/successor carve-outs.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "without the prior written approval of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld" — the reasonableness standard attaches to the approval requirement in both directions, including Customer's approval of a Vendor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor prohibition appears in the rendered clause; Vendor could assign to a Customer competitor if Customer's approval were given or if the assignee qualified as a Vendor affiliate/successor under the carve-outs. Operative language adding "and in no event to a competitor of Customer" is absent.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the rationale records (and the cited text confirms) that no change-of-control or deemed-assignment language exists in Section 15 or in the term/termination provisions, so no Vendor termination or re-pricing right is triggered by Customer's change of control and nothing needed deleting.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall assign ... except no approval is required for assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, upon written notice, to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets" — the exception is symmetrical, so each party may assign to a successor.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: "or, upon written notice, to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets" — notice condition is expressly attached to the successor carve-out.
Retained original language: "without the prior written approval of the other party" governs all assignments outside the affiliate and successor carve-outs.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted "which shall not be unreasonably withheld" immediately qualifies the prior-written-approval requirement, so the reasonableness standard governs all consent-requiring assignments.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete in operative language: mutual successor carve-out on written notice, retained consent requirement for other assignments, and an express reasonableness standard on that consent.

Preferred level is not reached: the successor trigger omits "acquisition" (only "merger or sale of substantially all assets"), and there is no prohibition on Vendor assigning to a Customer competitor. These are acceptable gaps given the claimed fallback target, but the finding should not be described as preferred-compliant.

The claimed status of deviation is correct on the original text: Section 15 as drafted required the other party's approval for M&A transfers and carried no reasonableness standard, failing two material fallback terms.

Minimal: the edit inserts only the reasonableness qualifier and the successor carve-out, retains the favourable pre-existing affiliate exception verbatim, and adds no survival tail, expense allocation, competitor bar, or procedural extras beyond the fallback checklist. The incidental deletion of "any of" and the tense change from "no such approval shall be required" to "no approval is required" are cosmetic and do not narrow Customer's position.

Preserves intent: mutuality, the affiliate carve-out, and the approval mechanic all survive without contradiction; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced, and no change-of-control or deemed-assignment provision elsewhere is disturbed.
Margin comment accurately states what changed and identifies the position as the fallback, consistent with the rendered text.
